name: Lusi

catalog_quote: Except in words of Anêm origin, stress tends to be penultimate, but in Anêm borrowings, the stress occurs on the same syllable as it does in the Anêm word pronounced in isolation.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.recode_to: Keep penultimate (penultimate stress). Consider dropping 'strict'/lexical_stress='no' in favour of 'penultimate with a lexically specified (Anem-origin) exception stratum' if the catalog counts loan strata: Thurston 1982:66,69,93 says stress 'tends to be' penultimate, that Anem-origin words (a 'significant proportion' of the vocabulary, incl. the whole /-ka-/ verb class) keep Anem stress placement, and that Counts' description 'must be revised to account for.. stress on other than penultimate syllables'.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the record's only quotation (domain quote, Thurston 1982) is confirmed verbatim in the held at printed p. 93 (PDF 103); the /-ka-/ passage at p. 66; the 'not attested as phonemic' sentence cited in the locator is about Anem (p. 92), not Lusi. Deciding source: the classification itself is database-derived (StressTyp2 < Gordon 2002 < Thurston 1982), with the stress quote/cite fields empty even though we hold and have verified a primary statement; hence upgrade-evidence-grade: cite Thurston 1982 PL B-83:93 (and PL B-99:34, 'stress is usually penultimate in all languages' of NW New Britain for isolated words) directly, fix the Anem/Lusi misattribution of the 'non-phonemic' line, and add a caution on the Anem-origin stratum with non-penultimate stress. Penultimate placement is not in doubt (Thurston 1982, Thurston 1987, Gordon 2002, and the sister language Kove per Sato 2013

sources.quote: For KOVE (closest relative, mutually intelligible with Lusi per Counts 1969): 'Primary stress always falls on the penultimate syllable ... Secondary stress falls on every second syllable to the left ... The stress rule in Kove is very strict. I have not found any exceptions.' Also states Counts 1969 'is actually a grammar of Lusi (Kaliai)'. Indirect support only; says nothing about Lusi stress itself.

sources.note: The only reference grammar of Lusi and the phonology description Thurston 1982 explicitly defers to ('Details of Lusi phonology are given in Counts 1969'); our classification rests on StressTyp2 plus a one-sentence appendix statement. Thurston p. 69 implies Counts states regular penultimate stress; reading it would give the primary stress rule, secondary stress, and whether non-penultimate items are noted.
